analysis.title: 11/9 Mkt Internal Insight: Strongest Bullish Setup YTD: Expect SPX 10%+ Higher in 3M
key_insights: UBS sales desk (Rebecca Cheong) expects SPX at least +10% higher over the next three months in a lower-volatility grind higher, citing washed-out systematic positioning.

Risk Control exposure is 55%, the lowest since the April 2025 tariff selloff. The last two comparable washouts were 55% on Aug 6, 2024 and 30% on Apr 10, 2025, after which SPX rose +17% and +24% over 4 months.
CTA global equity exposure is -5% (5th percentile vs 1Y, 23rd vs 5Y). Negative CTA exposure has historically been a bottoming signal, especially when real-money investors are not selling.
The desk argues the downside feedback loop is largely removed. Negative headlines can still trigger discretionary selling, but systematic funds are unlikely to amplify a move lower.
Real-money support comes from retail, foreign investors and corporate buybacks, which return next week. The desk expects news-driven selloffs to be shallow.

The desk's setup combines washed-out systematic positioning, limited incremental systematic selling, resilient real-money demand, short squeeze risk and potential CTA and Risk Control re-risking on the upside.

The author's weekend call of a Monday low was wrong because buying forces overwhelmed Risk Control, the one remaining systematic seller. The desk expects very little systematic selling left after today.
Intraday excess flow as of 1:00pm: +$34bn buying in S&P 500 with SPY +2.4%, and +$60bn buying in Nasdaq with QQQ +3.2%. Nasdaq buying is led by single stocks, likely retail demand and short covering.
Leverage ETFs are estimated to buy +$24bn, of which $20bn is in QQQ and tech ($10bn semis, $8bn QQQ, $2bn other tech).

Multi-strat funds may have cut risk during Asia hours as the spike in realized volatility pushed some pods toward risk limits. Risk Control is estimated to sell only about $5bn at SPX +2.4%, against $85-115bn of selling estimated for the day.

CTAs have barely bought so far today. Five buy triggers each sit for ES1 between 7654.6 (+1.2%) and 7715.9 (+2.0%) and for RTY1 between 2849.7 (+0.5%) and 2925.9 (+3.1%). NQ1 has no close buy triggers.

sector_views.rationale: The desk reports leveraged ETF buying concentrated in semis ($10bn), with the largest buys in NVDA, AMD, MU and AVGO. This is a flow observation, not a rating.

UBS PB L/S ratio is 1.91x, in the 2nd percentile vs 1Y.
Short squeeze: the UBS short basket (UBXXSHRT) is +4.10% so far today.
Nasdaq cash volume is 142% of average. S&P 500 cash volume is slightly below average. NQ1 and ES1 futures volume are at 125% and 119% of average.
UBS RMM client flow went from the 9th percentile vs 3Y to the 73rd and climbing. Friday's buy flow was in the 88th percentile.
Foreign-listed US ETFs bought every day last week, with weekly flow at +2.4x standard deviation.
